text:
mira: FYI brought reranker rv5 into staging for holdout_v5. Summary: overall NDCG@10 +0.7% but long-tail MRR@10 (freq_bucket=low) down -2.5%. Posting quick slices and experiments for triage.

oscar: Can you paste the slice breakdown?

mira: paste: 
```
slice            ndcg10   mrr10   top1_rate
overall          +0.7%    -0.2%   -0.4pp
high_freq        +1.1%    +0.5%   +0.8pp
medium_freq      +0.4%    -0.1%   -0.3pp
low_freq (tail)  +0.3%    -2.5%   -3.9pp
```
Notes: rv5 introduced candidate_truncation=200 tokens, and a prompt_priming prefix that appends the query summary to candidate text. Also onboarded hybrid-quant (int8 weights + fp16 activations).

jen: Interesting pattern: NDCG up slightly but tail MRR drops and top1 down substantially. Could candidate_truncation chop out anchor sentences for long documents that only match rare queries?

oscar: Also prompt_priming might be shifting probability mass if it boosts candidates with query overlap in longer docs differently. For tail queries the match is often an exact phrase earlier in the doc and truncation could remove it.

metrics-bot: Quick stat: low_freq candidates with match_position>200 tokens increased from 12%->29% after truncation. top1_prob for those candidates dropped ~6.1pp.

mira: Good catch. So truncation is chopping matches further down and prompt_priming isn't compensating for removed anchors.

jen: We should run a targeted ablation: (A) keep rv5 but set candidate_truncation=none (full) (B) rv5 with truncation=200 + remove prompt_priming (C) rv5 with truncation=400 (longer window) (D) legacy model baseline. Compare low_freq MRR and top1.

oscar: Also test hybrid-quant off to rule out quant interaction. Small chance quantization amplifies instability for low-signal tail.

mira: Queued eval jobs with eval_harness: 
```
./eval_rerank --model rv5 --dataset holdout_v5 \
  --trunc {none,200,400} --priming {on,off} --quant {hybrid,fp16}
```
ETA ~16m.

metrics-bot: Job 981 queued.

ops-bot: Reminder: hold Dedicated rollout pending triage for rv5.

metrics-bot: Job 981 results:
- A (trunc=none, priming=on, quant=fp16): low_freq MRR delta = +1.9% vs baseline (i.e. recovered).
- B (trunc=200, priming=off, quant=fp16): low_freq MRR delta = +0.4% (partial recovery).
- C (trunc=400, priming=on, quant=fp16): low_freq MRR delta = +1.5% (near recovery).
- D (trunc=200, priming=on, quant=hybrid): extra -0.6pp vs same with fp16.

jen: So primary driver = truncation (removing anchor spans), priming only helps if text remains. Increasing truncation window or disabling truncation recovers tail MRR. Quantization contributes small negative delta.

oscar: Actionable: for now set candidate_truncation to 400 for production for rv5 and keep prompt_priming on. Also file a follow-up to implement anchor-aware truncation: prefer keeping first/anchor paragraphs and local window around query-match positions when available.

mira: Filed rollout: https://go/rollout/rv5-truncation-fix (5% -> 25% -> 100%) with safety window 3h.

jen: Also add a small offline test to compute match_position distribution per bucket before any truncation patch in PRs. We should catch these regressions in the model onboarding checklist.

oscar: For quant: we'll keep hybrid-quant but add a small calibration for tail-weighted slices; follow-up ticket created.

metrics-bot: Post-rollout A/B scheduled. Collecting low_freq MRR/top1 every 5m.

mira: Thanks all. Learned: truncation decisions can disproportionately harm long-tail queries even when aggregate NDCG improves. We'll prioritize anchor-preserving truncation and add unit checks.
